description: A stiff paper cut to fill the recess left inside a board after the leather turn-ins, so the inner surface sits level. A grade as thick as the turn-in, such as engineer's cartridge, suits the purpose and helps draw the board flat as it dries.
name: filling-in paper

source_ref.label: Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (1901), Chapter XII, p.152. Internet Archive.
Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (D. Appleton, 1901), Internet Archive
